 Awar D
1.

By the order dated 11.12.2024 of Hon'ble Ms. Justice Neena Bansal Krishna, file was remanded to the Tribunal after setting aside the award dated 18.05.2023, for adjudication of just compensation under section 163A of M.V. Act.

It was specifically observed in para No. 15 of the Order of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that " The learned Tribunal, therefore, fell in error in denying the compensation under section 163A M.V.Act by observing that the probability of negligence of the deceased cannot be ruled out".
2.

It is seen that file has been remanded for limited purpose of adjudication of just compensation under section 163A of M.V. Act and the issue agitated before Hon'ble High Court was only with respect to the quantum of compensation awarded by Tribunal.
Finding of the Tribunal with respect to issue No.1 being in favour of petitioners, thus remain intact and has not been interfered with.
Hence, case at length need not be discussed and only issue No. 3 needs to be decided afresh.

3. In short, as per the claim of the petitioner, on 27.09.2015 at about 11:00 pm, late Sh. Ashok Kumar was going on a motorcycle bearing No. DL-7SBZ-2608 alongwith Sh. Sher Singh, the pillion rider, from Delhi to Etah.
When they reached village Shahpur Qutub, their motorcycle collided with a stationary car bearing registration No. UP-16AB-4155.
As a result, they both fell down and the deceased Sh. Ashok Kumar suffered grievous injuries.
He was taken to Meraj Hospital and then referred to Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital.
Thereafter, he was referred to Lok Nayak Hospital, where he expired during the course of his treatment on 02.10.2015.
A GD entry dated 07.10.2015 was registered by the police, though no FIR was registered.
4. I have heard Sh.Pradeep Kumar, Ld. Counsel for petitioner and perused the record.
5. Petitioner have succeeded to establish on record that Ashok Kumar died due to road traffic accident & further issue No. 1 has already been decided in favour of the petitioners.

The present claim petition is filed under section 163A of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (herein after Act) by the petitioners and adjudication of just compensation under section 163A of M.V.Act is as discussed in succeeding paragraphs.
6. For grant of compensation on a claim petition under no fault liability, there are two requirement to be fulfilled by the petitioner.

At first, it has to be established that a vehicular accident had taken place, involving use of motor vehicle, resulting in injuries to the injured or deceased and further to what amount of compensation, he is entitled under law, depending on the injuries sustained in the accident.

ISSUE NO. 3 :
7.

Section 163-A M.V. Act is extracted herein under:-
"Section 163-A. Special provisions as to payment of compensation on structured formula basis- Kamal Singh vs Jagdish Prasad on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117411164/
2 (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorized insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or permanent disablement due to accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation, as indicated in the Second Schedule, to the legal heirs or the victim, as in the case may be. ......................................"
8. The Second Schedule of M.V. Act has been amended vide notification bearing No. S. O. 2022 (E)
dated 22.05.2018 issued by Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

Further, there is no challenge to the testimony of PW1 that all of the petitioners are legal heirs of the deceased.
9. In view of above, it is held that petitioners would be entitled for a compensation of Rs. 05 lakhs.
Accordingly, the issue No.3 is decided in favour of petitioners.

RELIEF :
10.

In view of the findings on the issues, this tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-
(rupees Five Lakhs Only) alongwith interest @ 7% from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of award, in favour of petitioners and against the respondent no. 3/insurer and same is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.
Entitlement, Apportionment and Disbursement 11.
The petitioners in this case are the wife and children of the deceased.
As per the testimony of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 i.e. Kamal Singh was major and he himself appeared in the witness box as PW1.
Rest of the petitioners are the wife and minor children of the deceased.

Accordingly, I am of the considered view that total award amount of Rs.5,00,000/- shall be shared by all the petitioners in the following manner:-
